candidates.working_medium: mixed seawater ions, dominated by Na+/Cl- with Mg2+/SO4^2-/Ca2+/K+ contributions
candidates.energy_origin: free energy of mixing between streams of different salinity

resource_context.concentration_note: uses bulk mixed-ion streams; no single-ion extraction required

notes: Attractive as a co-located energy-recovery lane because both streams can already exist at water infrastructure.
Net energy is system-specific; membrane resistance, concentration polarization, fouling, pumping and pretreatment must be debited.

candidates.energy_origin: natural free energy of mixing at freshwater-seawater interfaces

resource_context.concentration_note: seawater total dissolved solids ~35 g/L; Na and Cl dominate

notes: Thermodynamically renewable as long as the hydrologic cycle re-establishes the salinity gradient.
Ecological score depends strongly on intake design, estuary disturbance, membrane fouling control and discharge.

candidates.working_medium: protons and other mobile ions in hygroscopic materials
candidates.energy_origin: humidity / moisture gradient driving ion diffusion and surface-charge redistribution

resource_context.concentration_note: working ions are generated/mobilized in hygroscopic media rather than mined as feedstock

notes: Best established today for low-power harvesting and sensing rather than grid-scale power.
Useful control lane because the external energy source is explicit: atmospheric moisture gradient.

candidates.energy_origin: candidate concentration, membrane, redox, or selective-ion gradients; pathway-specific
notes: Abundant divalent ion; attractive for screening because much more concentrated than lithium.
A specific repeatable energy cycle must be defined before performance claims.

candidates.working_medium: HDO/D2O/deuterium-bearing aqueous chemistry, with optional D+ state after ionization
candidates.energy_origin: UNRESOLVED for net energy; established isotope separation can prepare feedstock, while spin/ionic harvest remains hypothesis

resource_context.deuterium_fraction_note: roughly 1.5e-4 of hydrogen atoms in VSMOW-scale water; ocean inventory is enormous but isotope is dilute

notes: Resource depletion is unlikely to be the first constraint; separation and state-preparation energy are.
Do not score abundance as energy. Any net-energy mechanism requires a separately identified gradient or nonequilibrium resource.

candidates.energy_origin: candidate concentration, membrane, redox, or selective-ion gradients; pathway-specific
notes: Less abundant in seawater than Na/Mg but still orders of magnitude above Li.
Needs a defined conversion cycle before ranking on energy performance.

candidates.energy_origin: candidate concentration, membrane, redox, or selective-ion gradients; pathway-specific
notes: Abundant divalent species, but precipitation/scaling chemistry can become an engineering penalty.
Treat mineral scaling as a process cost and maintenance burden.

candidates.energy_origin: primarily resource recovery / storage carrier; no free ambient energy follows from Li+ abundance

resource_context.inventory_note: very large total ocean inventory but extremely dilute

notes: Excellent electrochemical carrier in batteries, but seawater extraction is concentration-limited.
Recycling/circular storage is more attractive than treating ocean Li as a primary energy source.

candidates.energy_origin: externally supplied ionization work stored as electronic potential energy

resource_context.concentration_note: not a naturally available high-energy state at useful density

notes: Laboratory physics is mature enough to use highly charged ions as a control/reference.
Closed-cycle neutralization cannot return more energy than was supplied to create the charge state under conventional physics.

candidates.energy_origin: externally supplied ionization work unless coupled to a separate ambient source

resource_context.source: terrestrial helium, mostly recovered with natural gas
resource_context.renewability_note: nonrenewable on human timescales; helium can escape Earth to space

notes: Useful physics control but poor sustainability candidate for bulk terrestrial energy systems.
Scarcity and strategic uses should be treated as opportunity-cost/ecological-resource penalties.
